_comment: tasks.md 9.1 — every number here is reconciled against spec.md §3 (Non-Functional
Requirements) and plan.md §6 ADR-1's serialization exit criterion, NOT transcribed from
tasks.md's own prose. tasks.md 9.1's original text said 'web entry <5 kB gzip' — that figure
is RETIRED. See `webEntryGzipBytes.source` below for NFR-6's full revision record.
THIS FILE IS NOW THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for `webEntryGzipBytes`. The previous version of
this comment asked a human to keep this number identical to a constant in
test/packaging/web-bundle.test.ts — 'both must be changed together or they will silently
diverge'. They diverged: the gate's MEASUREMENT was corrected from a Vite library build to a
consumer app build (4dae7c0) and the benchmark was not, so the same NFR was reported at
9418 B against 9216 here and 7712 B against 7933 there — 1706 bytes apart, both passing.
A comment is not a mechanism. test/packaging/web-bundle.test.ts now READS this value through
benchmarks/support/budgets.ts, and both call sites measure through the one function in
test/packaging/helpers/web-bundle.ts. There is nothing left to keep in sync by hand.

traversalP95Ms.source: spec.md NFR-3: native traversal completes in < 2 ms for <=60 shapes (CI benchmark, p95).

cacheLookupP95Ms.source: spec.md NFR-4: synchronous cache lookup by composite key completes in < 0.2 ms (CI benchmark, p95).

serializationP95Ms.source: plan.md §6 ADR-1 exit criterion: 'p95 serialization > 25% of the 2 ms budget on the 60-shape reference screen reopens this ADR' — 25% of NFR-3's 2 ms budget = 0.5 ms. Reported as a SEPARATE line item from traversal per ADR-1's own requirement ('the benchmark reports serialization separately so the trigger is observable').

serializationRatioOfTraversalBudget.source: plan.md §6 ADR-1 exit criterion, expressed as the ratio directly (serializationP95Ms / traversalP95Ms must stay < this value).

droppedFramesPerScroll.source: spec.md NFR-1: tier-1 sustains 60 fps / tier-2 sustains 120 Hz; fails if fps drops below target for more than 5% of sampled frames during the CI 50-cell scroll benchmark. Expressed here as the frame-drop-count tolerance for that same scroll.

webEntryGzipBytes.source: spec.md NFR-6, and the ONLY home of this number — test/packaging/web-bundle.test.ts and benchmarks/support/web-benchmarks.ts both read it from here. Record: (1) REVISED 2026-08-27 from 5 kB -> 8 kB by maintainer decision, after the first real measurement showed 7566 B and the original 5 kB was never validated against an implementation. (2) REVISED 2026-08-28 from 8 kB -> 9 kB by maintainer decision: the 8 kB gate did its job (it forced a design decision instead of letting the bundle grow silently) but the decision it forced — a per-platform typed-hint API divergence, no `<AutoSkeleton.Hint>` on web — is a worse outcome than ~250 bytes for a library whose entire proposition is 'one package, all platforms'. (3) CORRECTED 2026-08-29 (G.18), 9216 -> 7696: not a relaxation, the RULER was wrong. Vite library mode sets minifyWhitespace:false so 910 lines of this package's own doc comments shipped into the measured artifact — a number no consumer ever downloads. Re-derived to keep the gate exactly as strict: 8995 B measured against 9216 was 221 B of real headroom, and 7475 + 221 = 7696. (4) RELAXED 2026-08-29, 7696 -> 7933, by maintainer decision — this one IS the budget moving, and a fifth change must argue against BOTH precedents. It bought two real user-facing defects that had no gate (an empty 0-shape snapshot cached and replayed forever; a handoff handle destroyed only on unmount, announcing loading while painting nothing) for 99 B: 7613 -> 7712, set to 7712 + 221 to restore the same working headroom the corrected gate began with. (5) MOVED HERE 2026-08-30 from test/packaging/web-bundle.test.ts's NFR6_BUDGET_BYTES — same value, one home, because two homes is precisely how it silently diverged. HARD FAILING GATE. (6) RELAXED 2026-09-12, 7933 -> 8164, by maintainer decision. Record (4) required a fifth change to argue against BOTH precedents, so: it buys ONE real user-facing defect that had no gate — a `SkeletonProvider` theme change never reached an already-mounted overlay on web, so a dark-mode toggle left every skeleton on screen in the old palette until it happened to unmount. That is the SAME defect both native platforms already fixed (`setTheme` in AutoskeletonRendererTier1.kt / .swift); web was the one surface left without the channel, and `RendererHandle` had no theme method at all. Cost: 13 B (7930 -> 7943). Against precedent (2), which relaxed rather than accept a per-platform API divergence: this is the same argument and the same direction — refusing it would have left web permanently behind native on a documented theming contract. Against precedent (4), which is the one that moved the budget for 99 B: this is 13 B for a defect of the same class, and it was NOT reachable by making the code smaller — factoring the two setters into one helper measured WORSE (7956), because gzip already compresses the duplication better than a closure, and the only other unfoldable NODE_ENV read in the graph (createShimmerClock.subscribe) must ship, since it warns WHEN NODE_ENV IS production. The +221 is not padding: record (4) set the budget to measurement + 221 to 'restore the same working headroom the corrected gate began with', and 7933 had decayed to 3 B of headroom, at which point the gate stops measuring careless growth and starts measuring luck. Same formula, same intent. HARD FAILING GATE.

maxRegressionRatio.source: NOT spec-sourced — this session's own choice for the same-CI-job baseline-vs-candidate ratio gate (tasks.md 9.1: 'same-CI-job baseline-vs-candidate RATIO comparison'). spec.md/plan.md specify absolute budgets only; plan.md §7 says only 'measuring baseline and candidate in the same job on the same runner and comparing the ratio' without pinning a numeric threshold. 1.5x (50% slower than baseline) is a deliberately loose noise-tolerant gate for a CI runner with unknown headroom — a maintainer with real CI variance data should tighten this.

nativeHeapGrowthBytesRecycleStress.source: Promoted from examples/bare-rn's PaintGateListInstrumentedTest.kt MAX_NATIVE_HEAP_GROWTH_BYTES (12 MiB), task 6.4. See that file's own doc comment for the honest caveat: a two-point Debug.getNativeHeapAllocatedSize() sample on an ART-managed heap is not authoritative leak detection — it catches a monotonic unbounded climb, not a slow leak. Task 9.3 promotes this constant to a shared budget so the library test and any future CI wiring cannot silently diverge.
